companyDescription: Launch + space systems · Electron/HASTE operational, Neutron debut targeted Q4 2026 · $2.2B backlog · Q2 2026 earnings Aug 6
priceNote: Down 5.32% today per live-prices.json cache (1.4h old). Stock has pulled back roughly 30-34% from its late-May peak (~$151) amid Blue Origin test-failure spillover and SpaceX-IPO-driven sector rotation — not company-specific bad news.
summary: Rocket Lab posted a record Q1 2026 (revenue $200.3M, beat consensus, backlog surged to $2.2B on 31 new Electron/HASTE contracts plus 5 Neutron launch agreements) and the stock briefly broke $100 for the first time on the print before giving back gains over following weeks amid broader high-beta/space-sector volatility unrelated to Rocket Lab's own execution. Q2 2026 earnings land Aug 6 — management has guided another record quarter. Consensus target ~$108 implies ~41% upside from the current pulled-back price. Neutron's first launch (Q4 2026) is the bigger structural catalyst but sits further out.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Reports Aug 6, 2026. Management guided Q2 revenue of $225-240M (33-35% GAAP gross margin) — another record quarter if delivered. Q1's beat briefly sent the stock through $100 for the first time; a repeat clean beat plus reiterated/raised guidance is the near-term catalyst.

catalysts.name: Neutron First Launch
catalysts.description: Rocket Lab's medium-lift, partially reusable Neutron rocket — the real structural catalyst that would validate RKLB as a genuine alternative in a thinning medium-lift market. 5 commercial launch contracts already signed before first flight. Target: Q4 2026, watch for 'items on test stands' progress updates per CEO Peter Beck.

catalysts.name: Ongoing Contract Momentum
catalysts.description: Recent partnerships with Anduril and Raytheon, plus a new robotics acquisition, add to the $2.2B backlog outside the earnings/Neutron calendar.

risks: Rich valuation — ~40x estimated 2028 EV/revenue means a lot of good news is already priced in even after the pullback; a lot has to keep going right
Neutron has already slipped once (originally targeted earlier in 2026, now Q4) — further slippage is a real, repeatable pattern risk in the launch industry, not a one-off

High-beta and sentiment-driven — the ~30-34% pullback from the May peak was driven mostly by sector-wide factors (Blue Origin test failure, SpaceX IPO speculation pulling capital), showing this stock trades on more than its own fundamentals
Earnings reactions cut both ways — the Q1 2026 beat triggered a sharp pop, but a Q2 miss or guidance disappointment after such a strong setup could trigger a comparably severe drawdown
Dense macro event week (FOMC + 4 Mag-7 earnings + PCE, Jul 27-Aug 1) sits between now and the Aug 6 print — high-beta names are the most exposed to a risk-off shock in that window

estimateDates.note: Guided $225-240M revenue, 33-35% GAAP gross margin — another record quarter if delivered
5 commercial contracts already signed pre-flight — the structural re-rate catalyst

analystTargets.note: Highest named target — supporting color only

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed holds at 3.50-3.75%, but Chair Warsh's hawkish Jun debut FOMC (9/18 officials projecting a 2026 hike) keeps high-beta, high-multiple growth names like RKLB exposed to a higher-for-longer repricing.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core PCE accelerated to 3.4% YoY (May) — reinforces the hawkish setup into the Jul 28-29 FOMC, which lands one week before RKLB's own Aug 6 earnings.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: HIGH — RKLB already demonstrated ~30%+ sensitivity to sector sentiment shocks unrelated to its own fundamentals (Blue Origin failure, SpaceX IPO chatter). A genuine risk-off tape would likely hit this name harder than the market.
macroRisk.summary: Fed risk MEDIUM — the Aug 6 earnings catalyst is company-specific, but RKLB's demonstrated high-beta behavior and rich valuation make it unusually exposed to the dense Jul 28-Aug 1 FOMC/earnings/PCE week that lands just before its own print.

entryStrategy.verdict: BUY the pullback into Q2 earnings — Rocket Lab's fundamentals (record backlog, guided another record quarter) haven't changed, the ~30% drawdown from the May peak is mostly sector sentiment. Aug 6 is the near-term proof point.

catalystSpot.preRunup: Space-launch names with strong backlogs tend to run into earnings on guidance optimism, though RKLB's own recent pattern shows gains can evaporate quickly on unrelated sector news even after a strong print.
catalystSpot.preRunupPct: +5% to +15% typical pre-earnings drift, though sector volatility can override this

postWin.note: RKLB's own Q1 2026 beat sent the stock up 34% the same day, breaking $100 for the first time — a real, same-company, same-year precedent for how sharply this stock can react to a clean beat.

postLose.note: RKLB's own May 2026 print (a different quarter within the same cycle) also showed a case of the stock trading down ~7% on earnings despite record revenue — guidance quality matters more than the headline beat/miss for this name.

spotSizing.reason: Speculative sizing — real backlog and revenue growth support the thesis, but rich valuation (~40x 2028 EV/revenue) and demonstrated high-beta sector sensitivity argue against a larger core-holding-style position.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Below Entry 2 zone before earnings = momentum turning

stopPostCatalyst.note: If Q2 misses guidance or Neutron timeline slips further, exit within 2 sessions
